correctness.rationale: The claim is the simplicial complex of all 9-point F3² subsets avoiding any of the 12 affine lines, not a complex of maximal caps. An independent integer-mask calculation exhausted all 511 nonempty subsets and obtained 171 faces f=(9,36,72,54). The prescribed 79 matching pairs are disjoint; all 504 nonempty-face Hasse incidences were oriented and the resulting DAG completely topologically sorted. Exactly critical (C0,C2,C3)=(1,1,11) survive. Independently reconstructed exact signed integral Morse C3 -> C2 boundary is the 11x1 ZERO matrix, giving nullhomotopic 3-cell attachments to the unique S² since π2(S²)=Z. Therefore the full homotopy type is S²∨11S³, not just mod-2 Betti ranks.

originality.rationale: The equivalently named Hesse configuration cap or AG(2,3) Steiner triple system independence complex is topologically distinct from the projective cap complex and from graph-metric Rips nerves of the Hesse incidence graph. Artebani–Dolgachev identify the nine flex points and twelve lines, but the geometric primary source does not supply this cap homotopy classification in inspected Section 2. The cap-set counting literature addresses sizes, not integral attaching maps. Resultary found the affine-plane incidence Rips wedge with sixteen spheres in dimensions 2 and 3, an entirely different face predicate. Priority qualified by unknown older enumerations/hypergraph-independence tables.
residual_risks: Older Steiner triple system enumeration/full-text sources might contain equivalent hidden homotopy data; no exhaustive proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The affine plane AG(2,3) is a uniquely familiar Steiner triple system and classical Hesse configuration. Computing the *full* torsion-free homotopy type of its line-avoiding complex, including the mixed dimensions S² and S³, yields an exact reusable baseline for cap complexes and distinguishes it from projective and incidence-Rips variants; not an arbitrary unmotivated subset statistic.
